title: Is there a logic capturing polynomial time on unordered structures?
area: Database theory and finite model theory
formal: Is there an effective logic whose sentences define exactly the isomorphism-invariant polynomial-time properties of finite unordered relational structures, with an effective polynomial-time evaluation procedure for every sentence?
context:
Use the standard effective notion of capturing a complexity class. Merely attaching semantic labels to all polynomial-time machines is insufficient. A particular candidate extension of rank logic is separately recorded.

This question was found through Wikipedia and compared individually with the existing candidate and archived records. The linked literature provides definitions and background; this import is not a completed research-card review.
why: The central descriptive-complexity question of characterizing feasible computation without supplying an arbitrary order.
